propositions.text: The appellants are Indian citizens appealing the RPD decision denying refugee status and protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX (the Appellants) are citizens of India appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) that they are neither "Convention refugee(s)" nor "person(s) in need of protection".

paragraphs.summary: The appellants, Indian citizens, appeal the RPD decision denying them refugee status and protection, as stated by the court.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed, the RPD decision is set aside, and the appellants are recognized as Convention refugees.
propositions.quote: I allow this appeal, set aside the determination of the RPD and am substituting with my own determination. The Appellants are "Convention refugee(s)".

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal, sets aside the RPD decision, and finds the appellants are Convention refugees.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in determining a viable internal flight alternative in several Indian cities.
propositions.quote: Based on my review of the evidence in the file, I conclude that the RPD member erred in her determination of a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in assessing a viable internal flight alternative in multiple Indian cities.

propositions.text: The appellants would be at risk from VHP members if relocated anywhere in India due to their interfaith marriage and lack of police protection.
propositions.quote: I find that the XXXX would be at risk from members of the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) party if they relocated to Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, or Kolkata, or anywhere else in India, because of their interfaith marriage, and that they would not receive adequate protection from the police.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellants face risk from VHP members and lack police protection if relocated anywhere in India due to their interfaith marriage.

propositions.text: The appellants relied on Mr. XXXX's narrative and testimony of Mr. and Mrs. XXXX about persecution fears.
propositions.quote: The Appellants all relied on Mr. XXXXBOC narrative and the testimony of both Mr. and Mrs. XXXX.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX is a Muslim man fearing VHP due to his marriage to a Hindu woman, Mrs. XXXX.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXXis a Muslim man who fears members of the VHP, a right-wing Hindu extremist group. This group targeted Mr. XXXXbecause of his marriage to a Hindu woman, Mrs. XXXX.

propositions.text: The appellants claim persecution due to being Muslim and their interfaith marriage in India.
propositions.quote: In addition, the XXXXare claiming persecution by Indian society on the grounds of being Muslim in India and as a result of their interfaith marriage.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the appellants relied on Mr. XXXX's narrative and testimony about fearing VHP persecution due to their interfaith marriage and Muslim identity.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX was designated representative for his minor daughters before the RPD and RAD.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX was named as the designated representative for his minor daughters, XXXX and XXXX, before the RPD, and this designation was confirmed by the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD).

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found Mr. XXXX was designated representative for his minor daughters before the RPD and RAD.

propositions.text: The Minister intervened before the RPD on credibility but did not intervene in this appeal.
propositions.quote: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration Canada (the Minister) intervened before the RPD by filing submissions and documents on credibility, but has not intervened in this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Minister intervened before the RPD on credibility but not in this appeal.

propositions.text: The appellants submit the RAD should apply the correctness standard of review.
propositions.quote: The XXXX submit that the RAD should apply the correctness standard of review.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RAD should apply the correctness standard of review.

propositions.text: The RAD must independently assess all evidence and determine correctness of RPD errors of law, fact, or mixed law and fact.
propositions.quote: When reviewing the RPD decision, I am required to independently assess all the evidence and determine whether the RPD was correct in relation to each alleged error of law, fact or mixed fact and law.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the appellants on the standard of review.
propositions.quote: I agree with the XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the appellants that the RAD must independently assess all evidence and determine correctness of RPD errors.

propositions.text: The RPD correctly found discrimination from family and society due to interfaith marriage did not amount to persecution.
propositions.quote: The RPD's finding that the discrimination that Mr. and Mrs. XXXX said they experienced from family members and Indian society in general due to their interfaith marriage did not rise to the level of persecution is correct.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker correctly found discrimination from family and society did not amount to persecution.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX testified about resistance from family and society and workplace discrimination.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX testified that there was resistance from both their extended family and society, which made them feel unwelcome. He also explained that he had been discriminated against in the workplace.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found Mr. XXXX testified about resistance from family, society, and workplace discrimination.

propositions.text: The RPD analyzed discrimination claims separately from fear of VHP members in IFA analysis.
propositions.quote: The RPD analyzed this part of the claim distinctly from the XXXX fear of the VHP party members. As will be discussed below, her IFA analysis focussed on the XXXX fear of VHP party members.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the RPD analyzed discrimination claims separately from fear of VHP members in IFA analysis.

propositions.text: The RPD found resistance and social exclusion did not cumulatively amount to persecution as they were not basic human rights violations.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that Mr. XXXX testimony regarding feelings of resistance from family members and society and the absence of invitations "to a lot of social gatherings" did not cumulatively rise to the level of persecution, as those acts were not violations of basic human rights.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found resistance and social exclusion did not cumulatively amount to persecution as not basic human rights violations.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX alleged workplace discrimination and police bias due to his Muslim name.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX also alleged that he was discriminated by employers because of his religious profile as a Muslim. He testified that he was not given an opportunity to interview for "a couple of jobs" because the selectors were not Muslim and "probably put [my application] in the trash". He also testified that he would have received more help from the police in India if he did not have a Muslim name.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found Mr. XXXX alleged workplace discrimination and police bias due to his Muslim name.

propositions.text: The RPD found Mr. XXXX's allegations of job and police discrimination speculative and insufficient for persecution.
propositions.quote: The RPD found Mr. XXXX allegations that he was refused job interviews and police assistance because of his last name, speculative, and therefore, not sufficient to establish a serious possibility of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found Mr. XXXX's job and police discrimination allegations speculative and insufficient for persecution.

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD misunderstood their claim by focusing on family opinion and workplace discrimination.
propositions.quote: The XXXX argue in appeal that the RPD erred by misunderstanding the heart of their claim by presuming that the basis of their claim consisted of their family's opinion of their interfaith marriage. They add that the RPD erred by focussing on supplementary issues such as experiences of being discriminated against within the work force and barred from being allowed the opportunity for a job interview.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD misunderstood their claim by focusing on family opinion and workplace discrimination.

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD failed to assess incidents by a political party and did not do an individualized claim assessment.
propositions.quote: The XXXX further argue that the RPD failed to adequately address, by way of assessment, the incidents that had occurred against Mr. XXXX by an active and powerful political party, working under the very government in which the RPD expected Mr. XXXX to seek protection from. According to the XXXX, the correct assessment would be of their fear of being persecuted as a result of a national Hindu movement against Muslims. They add that an individualized assessment of their claim was not done.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD failed to assess political party incidents and did not conduct an individualized claim assessment.

propositions.text: The RPD did not fail to assess the appellants' primary fear of VHP persecution and national Hindu movement against Muslims.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the RPD did not fail to assess the XXXX primary fear of VHP party members and their fear of being persecuted as a result of a national Hindu movement against Muslims. The RPD member was not wrongly dwelling on supplementary fears, she simply analyzed them separately.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not fail to assess the appellants' primary fear of VHP persecution and national Hindu movement.

propositions.text: The RPD accepted past attacks and threats as credible and focused on forward-looking IFA analysis regarding VHP persecutors.
propositions.quote: By focussing her decision on a forward-looking assessment of a viable IFA, while considering the VHP party members as the persecutors, she accepted the XXXX allegations of past attacks and threats as credible. I disagree with the XXXX assertion that the RPD ignored the ultimate core of the claim. The RPD proceeded with a forward-looking analysis to determine whether an IFA was possible, given the past persecution by VHP members.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD accepted past attacks as credible and focused on forward-looking IFA analysis regarding VHP persecutors.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD that discriminatory behaviors did not cumulatively amount to persecution.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD's conclusion that the behaviours described by the XXXX, whether by their family members or in Mr. XXXX work life and his experience with the police in New Delhi, were discriminatory but that they did not cumulatively rise to the level of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that discriminatory behaviors did not cumulatively amount to persecution.

propositions.text: The RPD's assessment on this part of the claim is correct.
propositions.quote: The RPD's assessment on this part of the claim is correct.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in assessing the viability of an IFA in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata.
propositions.quote: The RPD erred in assessing the viability of an IFA in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's assessment partly correct but erred on the viability of an IFA in four Indian cities.

propositions.text: The RPD was incorrect in her IFA assessment; the appellants do not have an IFA in the named cities due to serious persecution risk.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the RPD was incorrect in her IFA assessment. The XXXX do not have an IFA in the cities of Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata or elsewhere in India because there is a serious possibility that they will be persecuted based on their religion and interfaith marriage.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's IFA assessment incorrect, concluding appellants lack an IFA due to serious persecution risk in those cities.

propositions.text: The IFA test requires appellants to prove serious persecution risk or personal danger in the IFA and that seeking refuge there would be objectively unreasonable or unduly harsh.
propositions.quote: This assessment is based on a two-prong test. Once the IFA has been raised, the onus of proof is on the Appellants to establish that: 1) there is a serious possibility that they will be persecuted in the part of the country identified as an IFA or that on a balance of probabilities, they would be subjected personally to a danger of torture or to a risk to their lives or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in the IFA; 2) the conditions in that part of the country must be such that it would be objectively unreasonable or unduly harsh, in all the circumstances, including those particular to the Appellants, for them to seek refuge there.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the two-prong legal test for IFA viability requiring proof of persecution risk and unreasonableness of refuge there.

propositions.text: The National Documentation Package on India has been updated since the RPD hearing and will be considered for country conditions and risk analysis.
propositions.quote: The National Documentation Package (NDP) on India has been updated since the RPD hearing in this file, and I will consider the updated information, especially on the country conditions with respect to Hindu extremism, in regards to my forward-looking analysis of the XXXX risk and the availability of an IFA.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes updated country information will be considered for risk and IFA analysis.

propositions.text: The court advised appellants it would analyze IFA in specified cities and disclosed the latest NDP, requesting further submissions.
propositions.quote: I advised the XXXX that I would be analyzing IFA, specifically in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata, as well as state protection. I disclosed the latest NDP and requested further submissions.

paragraphs.summary: The court informed appellants of its IFA analysis plan and requested further submissions with updated documentation.

propositions.text: The appellants responded with supplementary submissions and documentation on October 25, 2019.
propositions.quote: They responded to my request and filed supplementary submissions and documentation on October 25, 2019.

propositions.text: The court will address these supplementary submissions further below.
propositions.quote: These will be addressed further below.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants filed supplementary submissions which the court will address later.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellants did not face serious persecution risk in the proposed IFAs due to India's large population and geography limiting VHP's ability to find them.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the XXXX did not face a serious possibility of persecution in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, or Kolkata because the VHP members that attacked Mr. XXXX would not find them there due to the country's large population and geography.

propositions.text: The RPD added that the VHP would be hard pressed to know where to begin to look and would not have means to locate them outside New Delhi.
propositions.quote: She added that the VHP would be hard pressed to know where to begin to look. She specified that the VHP would not have the means to locate them outside of New Delhi.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no serious persecution risk in IFAs as VHP could not locate appellants outside New Delhi due to population and geography.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX testified that VHP has a wide network throughout India sharing information with its offices.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX had testified that the VHP organization was widely based and had a large network of members throughout the country, who give any information they have to the offices of the VHP.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX testified VHP has a wide network sharing information countrywide.

propositions.text: The RPD found VHP lacked ability or resources to locate appellants all over India, citing UK report on difficulty tracking individuals across states.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not find that this meant that the VHP had the ability or the resources to locate the XXXX all over India. She referred to a UK Country Guidance report that stated that it would be difficult for the police, or anyone, to track an individual in another state to which they had fled.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found VHP lacked resources to locate appellants nationwide, citing UK report on tracking difficulty.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellants had not established VHP motivation to locate them outside New Delhi.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that the XXXX had not established that the VHP would be motivated to locate them outside of New Delhi.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no evidence VHP was motivated to find appellants outside New Delhi.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX testified VHP member called him after first attack, knowing their new location; cousin saw VHP members near their house in 2018.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXXhad testified that after the first attack against him, on XXXX XXXX, 2018, and after he moved his family from New Delhi to South Delhi, a VHP member had called him and told him he knew where they had relocated to and that they could not hide from the VHP. Mr. XXXX also testified that his cousin told him VHP members were seen around their house in XXXX 2018.

propositions.text: The RPD noted appellants were never approached in South Delhi, failing to establish VHP ability to locate them in proposed IFAs.
propositions.quote: The RPD member noted that the XXXX were never approached in South Delhi, and that this further failed to establish that the VHP would be able to locate them in one of the proposed IFAs.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX testified VHP knew their location but RPD found no approach in South Delhi, failing to prove VHP could locate them in IFAs.

propositions.text: The RPD noted Mr. XXXX was unaware of anyone looking for them in New Delhi since 2018, indicating lack of VHP desire to track them elsewhere.
propositions.quote: In addition, the RPD also noted that Mr. XXXX was unaware of anyone looking for them in New Delhi since XXXX of 2018 and found that this pointed to a lack of desire on the part of the VHP to track them elsewhere in India.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no evidence of VHP seeking appellants in New Delhi since 2018, indicating no desire to track them elsewhere.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded appellants would not face serious persecution in the proposed IFAs.
propositions.quote: Based on the above, the RPD concluded that the XXXX would not face a serious possibility of persecution in the proposed IFAs.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD concluded appellants face no serious persecution risk in the proposed IFAs.

propositions.text: The appellants argue VHP has resources to find them and that corruption and VHP's movement to kill Muslims should be considered.
propositions.quote: In their memorandum of appeal, the XXXX argue that the proposed IFAs do not mitigate the fact that the VHP has the resources to find and locate them. They ask that the widespread corruption, bribery involved within the system and the VHP's strong-willed movement to kill Muslims, by way of Love Jihad, be considered.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue VHP can find them and corruption plus VHP's anti-Muslim movement should be considered.

propositions.text: Love Jihad is described as a movement targeting Muslim men marrying Hindu women for conversion and elimination.
propositions.quote: Love Jihad was described before the RPD as a movement (Love Jihad, also called Romeo Jihad, is an unsubstantiated campaign defined as an activity under which Muslim men target women belonging to non-Muslim communities for conversion to Islam by feigning love) where they target Muslim men who marry Hindu women and try to eliminate Muslim men.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants describe Love Jihad as a movement targeting Muslim men marrying Hindu women for conversion and elimination.

propositions.text: Appellants submitted articles on VHP actions against Muslims, systemic racism, and Love Jihad before the RPD.
propositions.quote: There were several articles in evidence put forth by the XXXX, before the RPD, on the VHP Party, their actions against Muslims and the systematic racism against Muslims in India which is not being stopped by the authorities, as well as the concept of Love Jihad and interfaith marriage.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants submitted articles on VHP's anti-Muslim actions, systemic racism, and Love Jihad before the RPD.

propositions.text: Appellants argue the country report relied on by RPD is outdated and similar to revoked IRB jurisprudential guide due to new information on police connectivity.
propositions.quote: In the supplementary submissions that I received, the XXXX refer to the country report that the RPD relied on to show that it was difficult for anyone to be tracked in India and argue that this was similar to the country information that supported an IRB jurisprudential guide that has since been revoked. They add that the reason it was revoked was because of developments in the country information, such as information on connectivity between police forces in India.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue the RPD's country report is outdated and similar to revoked IRB guide due to new police connectivity information.

propositions.text: Appellants argue they are unsafe anywhere due to Love Jihad targeting Muslim men and VHP's ties to ruling party.
propositions.quote: The XXXX argue that because of the Love Jihad phenomenon in India, they will not be safe anywhere, as Muslim men are being targeted for luring Hindu women, and Mr. XXXX has been personally attacked and threatened because of this in the past. They submit that this is even more so because the VHP has close ties with the ruling political party.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue they are unsafe anywhere due to Love Jihad targeting and VHP's ruling party ties.

propositions.text: Appellants argue recent citizenship amendment targets Muslims for exclusion and loss of citizenship.
propositions.quote: The XXXX also argued that because of a recent citizenship amendment in India, Muslims are being stripped of their Indian citizenship. They submit information and documentation about legislative attempts to isolate Muslims, which are being pushed through by the current political party, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). As such, they argue that should they return to India, they will face possible exclusion and loss of their citizenship.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue citizenship amendment targets Muslims for exclusion and citizenship loss.

propositions.text: The supplementary documentation submitted by appellants is accepted as new evidence meeting IRPA subsection 110(4) criteria and is relevant and credible.
propositions.quote: The supplementary documentation submitted by the XXXX, with their submissions dated October 25, 2019, is accepted as new evidence before the RAD as, in my opinion, it meets the criteria of subsection 110(4) of the IRPA and more precisely, is evidence that I requested when I asked for additional submissions on IFA and state protection. As such, the XXXX could not have been expected to produce it before the RPD. It is new information that is relevant to the issues of IFA and state protection in this claim, which are determinative, and the documents appear to come from credible sources.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts appellants' supplementary documentation as new, relevant, credible evidence under IRPA subsection 110(4).

propositions.text: Considered updated research, current NDP, and XXXX submissions and documents.
propositions.quote: I have considered the updated research and information contained in the most current NDP, as well as the XXXX submissions and supporting documents.

paragraphs.summary: The court considered updated research, current NDP, and XXXX submissions and documents.

propositions.text: XXXX argue they will be targeted by VHP due to interfaith marriage and conversion to Islam.
propositions.quote: the XXXX are arguing that the reason they will be located, wherever they go, is because of becoming a target of the VHP because of their interfaith marriage, and the fact that they are all now Muslim.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX argue they will be targeted by VHP due to interfaith marriage and conversion to Islam.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX was threatened and physically attacked in 2018 and police refused to take complaint.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX was first threatened over this on XXXX XXXX, 2018, but he managed to drive away. On XXXX XXXX, 2018, Mr. XXXX was physically attacked and beaten until he fell unconscious and required medical treatment. Mr. XXXX tried to report the matter to the police and he was rebuffed.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX was threatened and attacked in 2018; police refused to take his complaint, as the applicant reports.

propositions.text: Evidence shows XXXX identified by VHP and a hit list circulates encouraging attacks on interfaith couples.
propositions.quote: there is evidence that the XXXX have been identified by members of the VHP and that there is a hit list circulating on social media encouraging Hindu extremists to hunt down interfaith couples in India.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds evidence that XXXX are identified by VHP and a hit list circulates encouraging attacks on interfaith couples.

propositions.text: RPD relied on revoked IRB guide reasoning about tracking difficulties, but newer sources refute this.
propositions.quote: I agree with the XXXX that the country documentation relied on by the RPD about the difficulties in tracking an individual in India is similar to a line of reasoning found in the IRB jurisprudential guide that has been revoked.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD relied on revoked IRB guide reasoning about tracking difficulties, but newer sources refute this.

propositions.text: Corruption in Indian police means tracking depends on who searches and database access.
propositions.quote: The country documentation also reveals that corruption is rife within police forces in India and this leads to the conclusion that an individual could be tracked, depending on who was searching and if they could access the authorities' database.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police corruption means tracking depends on who searches and database access.

propositions.text: Concludes serious possibility of persecution for family due to religion even if relocated in India.
propositions.quote: I conclude that there is a serious possibility that this family could face persecution based on their religion, even if they were to relocate to one of the proposed IFAs, or elsewhere in India.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes serious possibility of persecution for family due to religion even if relocated in India.

propositions.text: RPD's decision on IFA analysis first prong was incorrect.
propositions.quote: The RPD's decision on this part of the IFA analysis was incorrect.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's decision on IFA analysis first prong was incorrect.

propositions.text: Because serious possibility of persecution established, second prong of IFA test need not be pursued.
propositions.quote: it is not necessary to pursue with an analysis under the second prong.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes second prong of IFA test need not be pursued as serious possibility of persecution is established.

propositions.text: No Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) exists in India for the XXXX.
propositions.quote: there is no IFA in India for the XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes no Internal Flight Alternative exists in India for the XXXX.

propositions.text: There is a presumption that a state is willing and able to protect its citizens adequately.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that a state is willing and able to adequately protect its citizens.

paragraphs.summary: There is a presumption that a state is willing and able to protect its citizens adequately, as a rule of law.

propositions.text: XXXX fear VHP; Mr. XXXX was threatened and attacked by VHP members; police refused to assist.
propositions.quote: The XXXX fear the VHP party, and Mr. XXXX was threatened and attacked in XXXX 2018 by members of this party on two separate occasions. The police refused to take his complaint or take any action to assist him.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX fear VHP; Mr. XXXX was threatened and attacked; police refused to assist, as reported to RPD.

propositions.text: RPD found adequate state protection existed in India for religious minorities within IFA analysis.
propositions.quote: The RPD found, within her IFA analysis, that adequate state protection existed in India for religious minorities.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found adequate state protection existed in India for religious minorities within IFA analysis.

propositions.text: State protection cannot be determined in a vacuum; linked to nature of persecution.
propositions.quote: state protection cannot be determined in a vacuum. The willingness and ability of states to protect their citizens may be linked to the nature of the persecution in question.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX argue state protection cannot be determined in a vacuum; it depends on nature of persecution.

propositions.text: VHP works with BJP to persecute Muslims; victims cannot expect protection from government.
propositions.quote: the VHP is not an ordinary person or group that can be tamed. Rather, this group is working hand in hand with the current government in power, the BJP, which is made up of Hindu nationalists and wish to wipe Muslims out of India.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX argue VHP works with BJP to persecute Muslims; victims cannot expect protection from government.

propositions.text: Presumption of protection in other areas is inadequate; forcing return violates Charter rights.
propositions.quote: forcing them to return to a country where they have proven fear of death by the Indian government is against their Charter rights.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX argue presumption of protection in other areas is inadequate; forcing return violates Charter rights.

propositions.text: VHP's close ties to BJP make them agents of persecution and state actors; CIA classified VHP as militant.
propositions.quote: their agents of persecution should be considered as Indian state actors. They add that in 2018 the CIA in the U.S. classified the VHP as a militant religious organization.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX argue VHP's ties to BJP make them state actors; CIA classified VHP as militant.

propositions.text: Because VHP are state actors, presumption of state protection is rebutted.
propositions.quote: because the VHP are state actors, they have rebutted the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The XXXX argue because VHP are state actors, presumption of state protection is rebutted.

propositions.text: Would not say VHP are state actors but strong connection exists between VHP and BJP.
propositions.quote: Although I would not go so far as to say that the VHP are state actors, it is clear from the documentary evidence that there is a strong connection between the VHP and the ruling political party, the BJP.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds strong connection between VHP and BJP but does not classify VHP as state actors.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX's police complaints were rebuffed and insulted; police said incidents were common and not worth time.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX attempted to file complaints with the police and was rebuffed and insulted. The police superior said this was a useless incident that was common and that they did not have time to waste on such reports.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Mr. XXXX's police complaints were rebuffed and insulted; police said incidents were common and not worth time.

propositions.text: No state protection for the appellants in India as prior protection attempts were dismissed without help
propositions.quote: there can be no state protection for the XXXX in India as they have already tried to seek protection and were dismissed without any action taken to help them

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no state protection for the appellants in India as prior protection attempts were dismissed without help.

propositions.text: Given current political climate and reports, appellants would likely not receive adequate state protection if relocated elsewhere in India
propositions.quote: it is more than likely that the XXXX would not receive adequate state protection elsewhere in India if they relocated

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants would likely not receive adequate state protection elsewhere in India due to political climate and reports.

propositions.text: Appellants have rebutted presumption of state protection for major Indian cities and rest of India
propositions.quote: the XXXX have rebutted the presumption of state protection for New Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata, as well as for the rest of India

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants rebutted presumption of state protection for major cities and rest of India.

propositions.text: RPD erred and was incorrect in determining a viable internal flight alternative (IFA)
propositions.quote: the RPD erred and was incorrect in her determination of a viable IFA

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in determining a viable internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Appellants established serious possibility of persecution by VHP if relocated to major cities or elsewhere in India, with inadequate police protection
propositions.quote: there is a serious possibility of persecution by members of the VHP if they relocated to Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Kolkata, or elsewhere in India, based on their religion, and that the police would not provide adequate state protection

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants face serious persecution risk by VHP and inadequate police protection if relocated in India.

propositions.text: Appeal allowed, RPD decision set aside, appellants recognized as Convention refugees
propositions.quote: I allow this appeal, set aside the determination of the RPD and am substituting with my own determination that XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXXand XXXX XXXX XXXXare "Convention refugee(s)"

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal, sets aside the RPD decision, and recognizes appellants as Convention refugees.
